title: Software Testing Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Software Testing lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Expected and actual results
entries.summary: A test compares an expected result with the actual result. A passing test only checks the case you gave it.

example.code:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(2, 3) === 5);

notes: One passing example is not proof that a whole program has no bugs.

entries.name: Choose useful cases
entries.summary: A test case includes inputs and the expected result. Choose cases that exercise different rules.

example.code:
const isFree = age => age < 5;
console.log(isFree(3), isFree(8));

notes: Do not test only many inputs that all take the same path.

entries.name: Boundaries catch small mistakes
entries.summary: A boundary is where a rule changes. Values just before, on and after it are especially useful tests.

example.code:
const canEnter = age => age >= 10;
console.log(canEnter(9), canEnter(10), canEnter(11));

notes: A greater-than sign and a greater-than-or-equal sign do different jobs.

entries.name: Empty input is a real case
entries.summary: An empty list has no items. Decide what your program should do with it before writing a test.

example.code:
const total = values => values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0);
console.log(total([]));

notes: Without the starting value, reduce on an empty array throws an error.

entries.name: Negative tests
entries.summary: A negative test checks how a program rejects an invalid input. The expected result may be a useful error instead of a normal value.
notes: Do not call an expected rejection a failing test.

entries.name: Unit and integration tests
entries.summary: A unit test checks a small part. An integration test checks parts working together. Each finds different mistakes.

example.code:
Unit: price(2, 3) returns 6
Integration: basket passes its items to the price calculator
End-to-end: a learner adds an item and sees the total

notes: Do not replace every small test with a slow whole-app test.

entries.name: Make a bug report useful
entries.summary: A bug report should let another person repeat the problem. Include steps, expected behaviour and actual behaviour.

example.code:
Steps: open quiz, answer 2 questions, press Next
Expected: question 3 appears
Actual: question 2 stays visible
Browser: the browser used for the test

notes: A report that only says broken does not explain how to reproduce the issue.

entries.name: Regression tests protect fixes
entries.summary: A regression happens when something that worked stops working. Add a test for a fixed bug so later changes check it again.

example.code:
Bug: empty basket crashed
Fix: use zero as the starting total
Regression test: empty basket total equals zero

notes: Do not remove the test as soon as the bug is fixed.

entries.name: Repeatable tests
entries.summary: A repeatable test gives the same result with the same inputs. Pass changing values in instead of hiding the current time in the calculation.

example.code:
const isLate = (due, today) => today > due;
console.log(isLate(5, 6));

notes: A test that depends on the real clock can change overnight.

entries.name: Explore with a question
entries.summary: Exploratory testing uses a goal and careful observation. You choose the next step from what you discover.

example.code:
Goal: can I use the search with only a keyboard?
Try: Tab to search, type a word, press Enter
Record: focus order, result, unexpected behaviour

notes: Random clicking without notes makes useful findings hard to repeat.

entries.name: Accessibility is part of quality
entries.summary: Accessibility means people with different needs can use the app. Test labels, keyboard access and visible focus as well as mouse clicks.

example.code:
Input label: Search lessons
Keyboard: Tab reaches input; Enter submits
Focus: a visible border marks the active control

notes: A color change alone may not explain an error to every learner.

entries.name: Report what was checked
entries.summary: A test summary says what ran, what passed and what remains unchecked. It should not promise more than the evidence supports.

example.code:
Checked: search, lesson links, quiz scoring
Passed: 14 cases
Failed: 1 keyboard case
Not checked: old browser versions

notes: Do not say all browsers work when only one browser was checked.
